title: lawcheck: drop instances that overflow the checker instead of failing the law; add --max-nat
description:
Bug (PLAN F31). Repro:
`bun tools/lawcheck/cli.ts research/candidates/mathlib-0.2/nat.bend --law pow_add --max-instances 20`
→ `! pow_add  error: Error: the machine stack overflowed (a deep recursion, or a literal too large to expand)`, exit 2.
Cause: random `Nat` values go up to 30 (`tools/lawcheck/src/values.ts`, `random()`, `case "nat"`), and
`Nat.pow(20n, 25n)` is far too big for the checker's unary naturals. The message comes from
`bend2/main.ts` and carries no `Location:` line, so `evaluate()` in `tools/lawcheck/src/checker.ts` (the
`loc === null` branch) marks EVERY remaining item of the batch as an error.

Change:
1. `checker.ts`: new Outcome variant `{ r: "toolarge" }`. In `evaluate()`, when `locate(out)` is null,
   the output contains `the machine stack overflowed`, and it is not a timeout: if `rest.length === 1`, set
   that item to `toolarge`; otherwise split `rest` into two halves and evaluate each half with the same
   function (recursively), merging the maps, then stop the loop. (Bisection finds the few huge instances
   with O(k·log n) extra runs.)
2. `lawcheck.ts`, `checkLaw`: instances whose claim evaluates to `toolarge` are dropped (neither pass nor
   fail); premises that evaluate to `toolarge` drop the instance too. Add `tooLarge?: number` to
   `LawResult` (set only when > 0). If every instance was dropped this way, the law is `skip` with reason
   `every instance was too large to evaluate (lower --max-nat)`.
3. New option `--max-nat N` (integer ≥ 1, default 30) in cli.ts `parseArgs` and `Options.maxNat`; pass it
   to the value generator so random `Nat`s are drawn from `0..min(maxNat, max(6, 3*size))` (today's rule
   with 30 replaced). The exhaustive small-scope phase is unchanged. Put it in USAGE and the README options
   paragraph.
4. Human output: append `, N too large to evaluate` to a law's line when `tooLarge` > 0.
5. README "Known limits": replace the sentence about random Nats staying ≤ 30 with the new behaviour.

Tests (`tools/lawcheck/test/lawcheck.test.ts`, real bend, no mocks):
- New fixture `tools/lawcheck/test/fixtures/pow.bend`: `import Base`, then law `pow_add` copied from
  `research/candidates/mathlib-0.2/nat.bend`, and a FALSE law
  `law pow_add_wrong:` with binders `a, m, n: Nat` and claim
  `{Nat.pow(a, Nat.add(m, n)) == Nat.add(Nat.pow(a, m), Nat.pow(a, n)) : Nat}` (false at a=0,m=0,n=0: 1 ≠ 2).
- Test A: `--json --max-instances 40`: `pow_add` status `pass` (not `error`); `pow_add_wrong` status `fail`
  with a counterexample; exit code 1.
- Test B: `--json --law pow_add --max-nat 3`: status `pass` and no `tooLarge` field (or 0).
Acceptance:
- `bun test tools/lawcheck` → all pass (existing 13 + new).
- The repro command above now prints `✓ pow_add …` and exits 0.
- `bun tools/lawcheck/cli.ts research/candidates/mathlib-0.2/nat.bend` → summary `46 laws: 46 ✓ · 0 ✗ · 0 ~ · 0 !`
  (paste the line).
- Planted negative: Test A's `pow_add_wrong` must still fail — dropping big instances must never hide a
  small counterexample.

title: reader: constructors written on one line (`A{} B{x: T} C{}`) fail to load or get the wrong line
description:
Bug in `@bendlib/reader` (used by lawcheck and the docs site). Real case: hub package
`0x05fa0e42448e8e221df592b204de523d`, `src/Wal.bend` line 64 `  PTag{} RLen{next: Phase} PKey{} PVal{} …`;
the docs site shows "The reader could not load this file".
Minimal repro — create `tools/reader/test/fixtures/ctors_one_line.bend` with exactly:
```
import Base

type Phase is Data:
  PTag{} RLen{next: Phase} PKey{}

def first() -> Phase:
  RLen{PTag{}}
```
`~/.bend/bin/bend tools/reader/test/fixtures/ctors_one_line.bend --check-only` → `All terms check.` (valid Bend).
`bun tools/reader/cli.ts tools/reader/test/fixtures/ctors_one_line.bend` → `…:3: Error: reader found no constructor 'PKey' after type Phase`.
Worse: before failing, `RLen` was matched at line 7 (its USE in `first`), not at its declaration on line 4.

Cause: `tools/reader/src/reader.ts` (around line 290, "ctor types carry no span of their own") finds each
constructor with the regex `(^|\n)([ \t]*)<Name>\s*\{` starting after the previous match: it requires the
constructor at the start of a line and can run past the type's body into later code.
Fix:
1. Bound the search to the type's body: from the end of the `type …:` header line to the first following
   line that is non-blank and starts at column 0 (the next top-level item) or end of file.
2. Inside that range, a constructor name matches when it is followed by optional spaces and `{`, and
   preceded by either line-start indentation or a `}` plus spaces on the same line. Keep in-order search
   (`from` = end of the previous match).
3. If a constructor is still not found within the body, keep throwing the existing `BendReadError` (never guess).
Tests (`tools/reader/test/reader.test.ts`): decls of the fixture list `PTag`, `RLen`, `PKey` as kind `ctor`
with line 4 and columns 3, 10 and 28 (1-based; compute them in the test with `indexOf` on line 4 to avoid
typos), and `first` as a def on line 6.
Acceptance:
- `bun test tools/reader` all pass; `git diff --exit-code tools/reader/test/golden` (goldens unchanged).
- `bun tools/reader/cli.ts tools/reader/test/fixtures/ctors_one_line.bend` lists the three ctors on line 4.
- `bun test tools/docs tools/lawcheck` still pass.

title: lawcheck mutate (1/3): mutation operators over one def's source text (pure, unit-tested)
description:
Why: mutation mode answers Bend's main criticism — laws too weak to pin the code (PLAN §0, §4.3). A law
set is strong for a def when every small change to the def breaks some law. This bead builds only the
pure part: generating mutated source texts. No bend, no files, no processes.

Create `tools/lawcheck/src/mutate.ts` (TypeScript, header comment ≤ 12 lines per AGENTS.md "Comments"):
```ts
export type Op = "arm-swap" | "arm-copy" | "literal" | "drop-succ" | "drop-cons" | "arg-swap" | "projection" | "base-swap";
export type Mutant = { id: string; def: string; op: Op; line: number; before: string; after: string; text: string };
/** 1-based [start, end] lines of `def <name>(`: its header line through its last non-blank body line. */
export function defSpan(text: string, name: string): { start: number; end: number } | null;
/** Every mutant of def `name`, deduplicated, none equal to the input text. */
export function mutants(text: string, name: string, params: string[]): Mutant[];
```
Bend source facts you need: top-level items start at column 0; a def's body is the following lines that are
indented or blank; `match x y:` lines are followed by `case <patterns>:` lines two spaces deeper, and each
case's body is the lines deeper than its `case` line. The def header may span lines (e.g.
`def List.reverse.go(…) ->\n  List<a, A>:`); the header ends at the first line ending in `:` at depth 0 of
parentheses. Never touch lines outside the span, `case`/`match` header lines (except as said in arm-swap),
text inside string/char literals, or text after `#`.

Operators, applied to body lines only:
1. arm-swap: for each `match` block, for each pair of its arms (i < j), swap the two arms' BODY blocks
   (case header lines stay). Only when both bodies are at the same indentation.
2. arm-copy: for each ordered pair (i ≠ j) of arms of one match, replace body i by a copy of body j.
3. literal: every standalone token `0n` → `1n`, `1n` → `0n` (not the `1n` of `1n+…`), `True{}` ↔ `False{}`.
4. drop-succ: an expression `1n+E` or `2n+E` on a non-`case` line → `E` (remove the `Kn+` prefix).
5. drop-cons: a top-level `A <> B` in a non-`case` line's expression → `B`.
6. arg-swap: in every call `f(x1, …, xk)` on a body line, swap each adjacent pair of TOP-LEVEL arguments
   (respect nested parentheses/braces/brackets); skip a pair whose texts are equal.
7. projection: replace the whole body by ONE line at the body's indentation holding each parameter name
   from `params`, then each of `0n`, `Nil{}`, `True{}`, `False{}` (one mutant each).
8. base-swap: whole-token swaps `Nat.is_le`↔`Nat.is_lt`, `Nat.is_ge`↔`Nat.is_gt`, `Bool.and`↔`Bool.or`,
   `&&`↔`||`, `Nat.min`↔`Nat.max`, `Nat.add`→`Nat.sub`.
Ill-typed mutants are fine: the runner (next bead) discards what the checker rejects.
`id` = `<def>#<n>` in generation order (operators in the order above); `line` = first changed line (1-based);
`before`/`after` = that line's old and new text, trimmed.

Tests: `tools/lawcheck/test/mutate.test.ts` (pure; reads fixture text with `fs`, runs no process):
- On `test/fixtures/lib_ok.bend`: `defSpan(text, "app")` is exactly the app def's lines; `defSpan(text, "nope")` is null.
- `mutants(text, "app", ["xs", "ys"])`: exactly one `arm-swap` mutant, whose text has `Push{c, app(r, ys)}`
  directly under `case Bot{}:`; six `projection` mutants; at least one `arg-swap` whose `after` contains `app(ys, r)`.
- `mutants(text, "size", ["s"])` contains a `drop-succ` mutant whose `after` is `size(r)` and a `literal`
  mutant turning `0n` into `1n`.
- For every mutant of both defs: lines outside `defSpan` are identical to the input; `text !== input`;
  all `text`s are distinct.
Acceptance: `bun test tools/lawcheck/test/mutate.test.ts` passes; `bun tools/comments.ts` exit 0;
full gate passes.

title: lawcheck mutate (2/3): run the laws against every mutant (killed / survived / invalid)
description:
Build the runner on top of `src/mutate.ts` (bead 1/3) and the existing engine in `src/lawcheck.ts`.
Read `tools/lawcheck/README.md` and `src/lawcheck.ts` (`lawcheck()`, `rootFor()` — the `--impl` swap —
and `checkLaw()`) first.

Add to `src/lawcheck.ts`:
1. Options: `shrink?: boolean` (default true; false → skip the shrink loop and the `?g` display step, report the
   first failing instance as is) and `firstFail?: boolean` (default false; true → check laws one after another
   and stop after the first law with status `fail`). Existing behaviour must not change when unset.
2. `export async function mutate(file: string, o: MutateOptions): Promise<MutateReport>` with
   `MutateOptions = Options & { def?: string }` (default `maxInstances` 50 when called from the CLI) and
   ```ts
   type MutantResult = { id: string; def: string; op: string; line: number; before: string; after: string;
     status: "killed" | "survived" | "invalid" | "error"; law?: string; detail?: string };
   type MutateReport = { tool: "lawcheck-mutate"; version: string; bend: string; file: string; impl: string | null;
     seed: number; maxInstances: number; tmpDir: string; defs: { name: string; mutants: MutantResult[] }[] };
   ```
3. Target file: `o.impl` if given; else, if `file` has exactly one local import (`import ./x.bend …`) and itself
   declares no def other than law fills, that import (impl mode); else `file` itself (in-file mode).
4. Target defs: reader decls of the target file (`decls(load(target), {scope: "own"})`) with kind `def` or
   `template`, excluding: law fills (a def named like a law), predicates (`predicate: true`), and defs whose
   type is an equation (`statement` set). `o.def` restricts to one (UsageError if absent).
5. In-file mode only: every mutant text (and the baseline) additionally has each law-fill def span removed
   (use `defSpan`), so the laws are open — otherwise the old proofs break under the mutant and the whole file
   fails to check (PLAN F8). Replace the removed lines with nothing; keep everything else.
6. Baseline: run `lawcheck` on the unmutated target (fills stripped in in-file mode). If any law is `fail`,
   throw `UsageError("the laws already fail on the unmutated code; fix those first")`.
7. Per mutant: write the text to `<tmp>/mut/<def>_<n>/<same basename as the target>` (a fresh directory per
   mutant so `--impl` basename matching works; nothing is ever deleted). Impl mode: `lawcheck(file, {...o,
   impl: mutantPath, shrink: false, firstFail: true})`; in-file mode: `lawcheck(mutantPath, {...})`.
   Classify: `ModuleError` or `BendReadError` thrown → `invalid` (detail = first line of the message);
   any law `fail` → `killed` (law = its name); every law pass/skip → `survived`; any law `error` → `error`.
   Mutants run one after another (each lawcheck run already uses all cores).

Tests (real bend; new fixtures in `tools/lawcheck/test/fixtures/`):
- `mut_weak.bend`: `import Base`, `import ./lib_ok.bend as M`, and only law `app_size` (copy from `laws_lib.bend`).
- `mut_strong.bend`: same import plus laws that pin both defs: `app_size`, `app_bot`, and
  `app_nil: for ys: M.Stack {M.app(M.Bot{}, ys) == ys : M.Stack}`,
  `app_push: for c: Nat, for r: M.Stack, for ys: M.Stack {M.app(M.Push{c, r}, ys) == M.Push{c, M.app(r, ys)} : M.Stack}`,
  `size_bot: {M.size(M.Bot{}) == 0n : Nat}`, `size_push: for c: Nat, for r: M.Stack {M.size(M.Push{c, r}) == 1n+M.size(r) : Nat}`
  (one binder per `for` line, as usual). First confirm with `bun tools/lawcheck/cli.ts` that all these laws pass on lib_ok.
- Test weak: `mutate(mut_weak.bend, {maxInstances: 40, seed: 1, size: 3})` → def `app` has ≥ 1 `survived`
  mutant and one of them has op `arg-swap` (`app(r, ys)` → `app(ys, r)` keeps sizes equal). At least one
  mutant overall is `invalid`.
- Test strong: same call on `mut_strong.bend` → zero `survived` for def `app` (`size` too, unless a survivor is
  a genuinely equivalent mutant — if so, assert on `app` only and name the equivalent mutant in a test comment).
- Test in-file: `test/fixtures/correct.bend` has laws and defs in one file; `mutate(…, {def: "dbl"})` runs
  without throwing and reports ≥ 1 killed mutant.
Acceptance: `bun test tools/lawcheck` passes (existing + new); paste the weak/strong summary numbers.

title: lawcheck: instantiate template function binders (~f, ~eq, ~le) from a catalog of closed functions
description:
Today `plan()` in `tools/lawcheck/src/lawcheck.ts` skips any law with a template binder of function type
(it throws `Skip("template binder ~f (v0.2)")`; the CLI prints it as `~ … skipped: template binder ~f (v0.2)`):
8 of list.bend's laws and every template lemma of mathlib 0.2. Note `plan()` stops at the FIRST such binder
(the `binders.find(...)` near the top); restructure it into the per-binder classification loop that follows
(one branch per binder kind), so a law with several template binders gets each one instantiated, and a
proposition-typed template binder still skips the law.
Templates take CLOSED functions (PLAN F12/F28: `~(x => g(f(x)))` works), so a small catalog of closed lambdas
per type can instantiate them.

Change:
1. After type parameters are instantiated (U32, then Nat), each function-typed template binder `~f: T1 -> … -> R`
   gets candidates from a catalog keyed by the instantiated signature. Start with:
   - `Nat -> Nat`: `(lc_x => lc_x)`, `(lc_x => 0n)`, `(lc_x => 1n+lc_x)`, `(lc_x => Nat.double(lc_x))`
   - `Nat -> Bool`: `(lc_x => True{})`, `(lc_x => False{})`, `(lc_x => Nat.is_le(lc_x, 1n))`
   - `Nat -> Nat -> Bool`: `(lc_x lc_y => Nat.is_le(lc_x, lc_y))`, `(lc_x lc_y => Nat.is_eq(lc_x, lc_y))`, `(lc_x lc_y => True{})`
   - `Nat -> Nat -> Nat`: `(lc_x lc_y => Nat.add(lc_x, lc_y))`, `(lc_x lc_y => lc_x)`, `(lc_x lc_y => lc_y)`
   - the same shapes for `U32` using U32 operations — FIRST check the U32 literal and operator syntax with
     `bend guide` and `bend base U32` and a scratch file that type-checks; drop any entry that does not check.
   Lambda parameters are named `lc_*` so `rewrite()` never hits `Shadowed`. Verify the multi-argument lambda
   syntax (`x y => …` vs `x => y => …`) against `bend guide` before writing the catalog.
2. The instance budget of a law is split across the product of its template binders' catalogs (cap: 8
   combinations, in catalog order). A signature not in the catalog → skip with reason
   `no catalog functions for ~f: <signature>`.
3. A binder whose type is a proposition about templates (e.g. `for ~assoc: …`) still skips:
   `template hypothesis (v0.3)`.
4. Counterexamples list template bindings like value bindings: `f = (lc_x => 1n+lc_x)`.
Tests (real bend): new fixture `test/fixtures/templates_map.bend` with a TRUE law (List<Nat> `List.length` of
`List.map` equals the length — copy `length_map` from packages/bend-mathlib/list.bend) → `pass`, and a FALSE law
`{List.map(~A, ~A, ~f, xs) == xs : List<A>}` → `fail` with `f` bound to a non-identity entry.
The existing fixture `test/fixtures/template.bend` and its test expect a skip today; if it now runs, update that
test's expectation AND say so in the commit message (a feature change, not a weakened test).
Acceptance: `bun test tools/lawcheck` passes; `bun tools/lawcheck/cli.ts packages/bend-mathlib/list.bend` →
fewer than 8 `~` and zero `✗` (paste the summary line).

  exits 0; `tools/lawcheck/test/fixtures/buggy.bend --max-instances 30` exits 1;

- length_replicate: `# Replicating x n times gives a list of length n.`
- length_range: `# range(n) has length n.`
- length_zip: `# Zipping two lists gives the length of the shorter one.`
